title: Claims Desk Guidance — Prepaid Dental HMO Plans Out-of-Area Emergency Reimbursement
content:
**Prepaid Dental HMO Plans — emergency palliative treatment by a non-network dentist.**

Emergency palliative treatment by a non-network dentist is reimbursed to the member only when the emergency occurred more than the plan's minimum emergency distance from the assigned primary care dentist and the receipt is submitted within the plan's emergency claim period in calendar days; the reimbursement is the amount paid up to the plan's out-of-area reimbursement maximum per incident.

Follow-up and definitive treatment must be done by the assigned primary care dentist; an emergency within the distance is treated by the assigned dentist at the palliative emergency copay and is not reimbursed.

**What decides a reimbursement**

| Input | Judgement | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Distance of the emergency from the assigned primary care dentist | More than the plan's minimum distance? | Not more: not reimbursed; such an emergency is treated by the assigned dentist at the palliative emergency copay |
| Date the receipt is submitted | Within the claim period, in calendar days after the emergency? | Not within: not reimbursed |
| Amount the member paid for the palliative treatment | Compared with the plan's per-incident maximum | Reimbursement is the amount paid, but no more than the maximum |

Both the distance condition and the receipt condition must hold for any reimbursement.

**The amount.** For one incident, the reimbursement is the lower of the amount the member paid and the plan's out-of-area reimbursement maximum per incident.

**Worked cases (hypothetical; minimum distance 50 miles, claim period 180 days, per-incident maximum 60.00 chosen for illustration)**

1. An emergency 120 miles from the assigned dentist; receipt for 48.00 submitted 30 days later. Reimbursed 48.00, the amount paid, which is below the maximum.
2. The same emergency with a receipt for 210.00. Reimbursed 60.00, the maximum.
3. An emergency exactly 50 miles from the assigned dentist. Not more than 50 miles, so not reimbursed.
4. An emergency 120 miles away; receipt submitted 200 days later. Outside the claim period, so not reimbursed.

**After the emergency.** Follow-up and definitive treatment must be done by the assigned primary care dentist.
